ground_truth: If a leverage token is created before a treasury address is set, its fee accrual timestamp is not initialized. When the treasury is later set, the first fee calculation uses a duration starting from the Unix epoch, leading to an excessively large, incorrect fee.

When the treasury address is not set, management fees accrue virtually. This unfairly dilutes new minters, as their deposit is valued against a total supply that includes phantom fee shares. It also penalizes redeemers, as the assets backing the phantom shares are redistributed to remaining holders, causing the redeemer to receive less than their fair share.

The `_redeemAndRepayMorphoFlashLoan` function takes the user's maximum shares upfront but fails to refund any unused shares if the actual redemption costs less. These leftover shares become permanently stuck in the contract[cite: 3086, 3098, 3104].
